limitations: Developer-run: the authors chose the tasks, the adapters, the layer-selection rule and the statistics, and ran every baseline.
Every accuracy number is a BF16 run. The released default is the INT8 engine, for which no accuracy value is printed.
Per-task values are printed for 13 of the 29 models only.

ProteinGym scores depend on the assays included, the aggregation, the checkpoint and the scoring code; this suite's ProteinGym protocol is its own and is not the leaderboard's, though the authors report reproducing eight leaderboard checkpoints to within 0.0025.
attributes.scope_note: 32 tasks run on 29 models (HyPLM-Flash and 28 public checkpoints from 13 families), all in BF16 through the authors' own adapters. Assembled and run by the developer of HyPLM-Flash, so every evaluation in it is author-reported and none is independent of the developer.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. All six pinned artifacts were re-downloaded at the pinned commit and their SHA-256 checked against the source records; pdftotext -layout reproduced the archived text layer byte for byte. npm run batch -- check-values was run over the whole batch (value-check.tsv). The 469 recorded cells of Tables 3, 5, 6 and 7 were then re-read by a reviewer script written for this pass, which takes each table's column order from its printed header line and splits every body row by printed cell, without using extract/parse.py; every printed value and column matched. The two arithmetic constraints were re-derived independently rather than taken from the extractor's checker: each Table 3 perplexity against exp of its NLL over the NLL's own rounding interval, and each Table 5 average against the mean of its five categories. Column assignment in Tables 6 and 7 is anchored outside those tables, by Table 3's NLL values and by Figure 3a's and Table 5's ProteinGym values, and the four printed paired differences reconcile with the Table 6 ProteinGym row. The 15 locators check-values cannot parse, four Figure 3a bar labels and eleven prose values, were read by hand against the text layer; in Figure 3a each bar label and its value share one line. extract/check_cells.py was rerun and reproduces cell-check.tsv.
review.reviewer_note: Claude research agent; no human review claimed. Reviewed by a different agent from the one that extracted the batch. Transcription checked against the pinned source; nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed.

attributes.condition: INT8 is applied per packed batch and only when the batch holds at least quant_min_tokens tokens (default 1,024; model.py lines 41 and 102). Smaller batches run BF16 although precision is int8, including a job's final batch when it falls under the threshold and every CUDA-graph bucket (64 to 512 tokens, graphs.py line 12), so the low-latency single-protein path always runs BF16. A configuration labelled INT8 does not run INT8 throughout.
limitations: No accuracy value is printed for this configuration: every accuracy result in the report is a BF16 run. Section 3 says INT8 keeps zero-shot fitness, structure, function annotation and likelihood within 0.01 of BF16, a list that omits regression, and the release recommends BF16 for regressors on near-identical variants. HyPLM-Flash's largest supervised margin over ESM-2 650M, AAV two-vs-many (0.650 against 0.518), is a regression task measured in BF16, so the INT8 cost on the task family with the headline margin is not measured anywhere in the release.

result_status.note: No accuracy result, on any task, is printed for the INT8 engine.

attributes.aggregation: One value per model on the test split
limitations: One GPU model (NVIDIA H20) on one workload. HyPLM-Flash runs an optimised engine and the baselines their reference implementations, so the ratio is against those implementations, not against equally optimised baselines.

The engine applies INT8 only to packed batches of at least 1,024 tokens (model.py line 102), so batches under that size run BF16 even when precision is int8; a workload of short batches would not run at this rate.

Only HyPLM-Flash's figure is printed. Baseline throughputs appear only as unlabelled points in Figure 1a and as ranges: Section 1 puts the reference implementations of recent 600M-class encoders at 48,000 to 69,000 residues per second, and Section 3 puts HyPLM-Flash 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than ESM C 600M, ESM-1b, ESM-2 650M, DPLM-650M and E1-600M.
attributes.metric_implementation: Each model uses the fastest attention kernel its implementation supports: FlashAttention-2 for ESM-1b, ESM-2 and DPLM, FlashAttention for ESM C and E1, xformers for AMPLIFY and PyTorch SDPA for ProtBERT and ESM3-open; HyPLM-Flash runs on its INT8 engine.
attributes.metric_qualifier: Residues embedded per second on one NVIDIA H20 for 2,048 held-out proteins (639,806 residues) in length-sorted batches of at most 16,384 tokens; HyPLM-Flash on its INT8 engine, where INT8 applies only to packed batches of at least 1,024 tokens

evidence_concerns.message: The recent-PDB likelihood panel is described two ways. Section 4.3 and the Table 3 caption give 887 PDB chains released after 2 September 2026; Table 4 gives 887 RCSB PDB entries released 9 September to 7 October 2026. The start of the window and whether the unit is a chain or an entry both differ, so the panel cannot be rebuilt from the report.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Section 4.3; Table 3 caption; Table 4 row 'PDB time split'

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix A states that the authors could not reproduce xTrimoPGLM's published ProteinGym scores (their runs fall 0.07 to 0.09 below the leaderboard) and that its likelihood is implausibly high, pointing to an incompatibility between their adapter and its masked-language-model head. They withhold its zero-shot and likelihood results and keep its embedding-based results as unaffected, but those results come from the same adapter and that claim was not tested.

Appendix A states that for GB1 two-vs-rest, GB1 three-vs-rest and the cross-protein hydrolase split of FLIP2, validation data come from the training distribution while the test sets are strongly shifted, so probe selection is dominated by noise and numerically equivalent runs of the same model differ by up to 0.2. The authors print these cells but leave them out of every summary statistic.

limitations: Author-released report, not peer reviewed. All three authors are at Tencent Hunyuan, which released the model, and every baseline was run by the same team through its own adapters; no result here is independent of the developer.

All accuracy results were computed with BF16 arithmetic. The released default is the INT8 engine, for which the report prints no per-task value; it states only that INT8 keeps zero-shot fitness, structure, function annotation and likelihood within 0.01 of the BF16 results.

Section 4 states that confidence intervals are paired bootstrap intervals, but the report prints intervals only for four ProteinGym paired differences. Every table cell is printed without its interval.

Tables 6 and 7 print every task for 13 of the 29 models only. The other 16 checkpoints appear at most in Figure 3a, Table 3, Table 5 or the prose, and 8 of the 28 public checkpoints are never named with a value, so the report's list of 28 cannot be reconstructed from it.
Table 5's rows without a dagger are published ProteinGym leaderboard values at commit 144fe22, quoted rather than run by the authors; they are not recorded from this source.

Throughput was measured on one NVIDIA H20 with the INT8 engine for HyPLM-Flash and with reference implementations for the baselines, each with the fastest attention kernel its implementation supports. Only HyPLM-Flash's own figure and the baselines' range are printed.
